name: og-07-ecology-before-luca
title: Ecology Before LUCA
question: In connected pore networks with cross-feeding, parasitism, cooperation and horizontal exchange, what emergent capabilities arise — compared to ancestral reconstructions, without assuming LUCA is primitive?
hypothesis: Heterogeneous populations develop metabolic diversity, cross-feeding and robustness single compartments do not; the emergent capability set overlaps the anaerobic H2/CO2/FeS LUCA reconstruction as a boundary.
objective: Run heterogeneous populations over a connected pore network; compare emergent capability redundancy (robustness) to the isolated counterfactual, and the collective repertoire to the LUCA reconstruction as a constraint.
proposed_models_methods: Vivarium multi-agent composites over shared spatial fields

conditions.name: reproducibility
conditions.expr: solver and db and seed and scenario recorded

behavior_tests.description: The metacommunity's collective capability repertoire overlaps the anaerobic H2/CO2/FeS LUCA reconstruction — reported as a far-end boundary the emergent set approaches, NOT a target the model is tuned to hit.

measure.detail: collective repertoire overlap with the anaerobic LUCA core (Weiss 2016)

literature_anchors.expectation: LUCA: anaerobic, H2-dependent, CO2-fixing, FeS-rich (355 protein families)
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Measured — collective repertoire overlaps the anaerobic LUCA core at ~0.6-0.7 (reported boundary)

claim: A connected metacommunity of heterogeneous pore compartments develops functional redundancy (robustness) that an isolated compartment cannot — cross-feeding and horizontal transfer spread coarse-grained protometabolic capabilities into >= 2-fold coverage, so most functions survive a single-compartment loss. Robustness EMERGES only in a bounded region of (cross-feeding exchange_rate x inter-compartment diversity) — too little diversity leaves nothing to share, too little exchange leaves a broad repertoire fragile. The collective repertoire's overlap with the anaerobic H2/CO2/FeS LUCA reconstruction is REPORTED as a far-end boundary the emergent set approaches (~0.6-0.7), not a target — LUCA constrains which capabilities are eventually acquired, not evidence the first compartments were LUCA-like.
result: Connected metacommunity robustness 0.667 (canonical seed) > isolated counterfactual 0.500; across 8 seeds connected 0.71±0.08 strictly beats isolated 0.42±0.06 on every seed (min gain 0.17). Collective LUCA-core overlap 0.60 (canonical), 0.70±0.14 across seeds — reported as a boundary.

findings.statement: A connected metacommunity of 8 pore compartments, each carrying a sparse coarse-grained protometabolic capability vector (2 of 12 functions intrinsic), develops functional redundancy (robustness 0.667) through cross-feeding and horizontal transfer, well above the isolated counterfactual (0.500) run on the identical seeded assignment. Across an 8-seed sweep the connected arm (0.71±0.08) strictly beats the isolated arm (0.42±0.06) on every seed (min gain 0.17), so the redundancy is a product of connectivity, not of the capability assignment.

evidence.observed: connected robustness 0.71±0.08 vs isolated 0.42±0.06 across 8 seeds, 8/8 pass, min gain 0.17

findings.explanation: Coarse-grained deterministic metacommunity (reproduction, not wrapped ALife). Cross-feeding (a compartment expressing a capability its neighbour lacks supplies the byproduct) and horizontal transfer (the capability is copied from a donor) spread sparse intrinsic capabilities into redundant coverage across the ring; a capability held by >= 2 compartments survives a single-compartment loss. Acquired capability decays toward the intrinsic set, so it persists only while continuously supplied.

findings.statement: Robustness EMERGES only in a bounded corner of (cross-feeding exchange_rate x inter-compartment diversity). At low diversity the compartments are near-identical, so cross-feeding/HGT have nothing to share and robustness stays at the sparse intrinsic floor (~0.17-0.25 regardless of exchange); at low exchange a diverse-but-disconnected set holds a broad repertoire fragilely (each capability in one compartment, ~0.33-0.42); only where diversity >= ~0.4 AND exchange crosses ~0.2 does robustness climb to 0.58-0.83. The transition is a phase boundary, not a monotone response to either knob alone.

evidence.observed: robustness landscape over (exchange x diversity): emergence boundary at exchange~0.2, diversity~0.4; canonical operating point 0.667

findings.explanation: Cross-feeding scales as exchange_rate/connectivity and is deficit-driven (zero between identical compartments), so diversity is the raw material and exchange is the spreading mechanism; both are necessary. The sparse capability space (2 of 12 intrinsic per compartment) makes an isolated compartment functionally fragile, so redundancy must be BUILT by the metacommunity.

findings.statement: The metacommunity's collective capability repertoire overlaps the Weiss-2016 anaerobic H2/CO2/FeS LUCA core at 0.60 (canonical) and 0.70±0.14 across seeds. This is reported as a far-end BOUNDARY the emergent set approaches from below — a phylogenomic constraint on capabilities eventually acquired — and is explicitly NOT a fitting target; the model is never tuned toward it.

evidence.observed: collective LUCA-core overlap 0.60 canonical, 0.70±0.14 across 8 seeds (reported, not gated)

findings.explanation: The LUCA reconstruction (anaerobic, H2-dependent, CO2-fixing, FeS-rich; Weiss 2016, 355 protein families; Moody 2024, LUCA embedded in an ecosystem ~4.2 Ga) is a constraint on which capabilities the lineage eventually acquired, used as a boundary condition on the emergent repertoire rather than as evidence the first compartments were LUCA-like.

report.title: Ecology before LUCA
report.verdict: PASS — a connected metacommunity builds functional redundancy a single compartment cannot, in a bounded diversity x exchange region; LUCA overlap reported as a boundary, not a target
report.main_insight: Connectivity, not complexity, is what makes a population robust before LUCA. Cross-feeding and horizontal transfer spread sparse protometabolic capabilities into redundant coverage across a pore network, so most functions survive a single-compartment loss — but only where diversity gives cross-feeding something to share AND exchange spreads it (a phase boundary). The collective repertoire's overlap with the anaerobic H2/CO2/FeS LUCA reconstruction (~0.6-0.7) is a far-end boundary the emergent set approaches, not a target.
report.conclusion: A coarse-grained, deterministic cross-feeding metacommunity shows that heterogeneous, connected pore compartments develop capability redundancy (robustness) a single compartment cannot — strictly, on every seed, above the isolated counterfactual run on the identical assignment. Robustness emerges in a bounded (diversity x exchange) region, so the result is a phase boundary rather than a trivial monotone gain. The overlap with the LUCA reconstruction is treated as a boundary condition on capabilities eventually acquired, never a fitting target — so the study does not assume LUCA was primitive. Opens the ecological era of the campaign ahead of og-08 (escape from the vent).
report.caveat: The capability vector and its exchange/transfer dynamics are coarse-grained couplings (a deterministic reproduction, not a wrapped ALife/agent engine, and not N instantiated libRoadRunner networks); the metacommunity dynamics are explicit and reproducible given the seed.

biological_validation.basis: Reproduces the ecological expectation that connected, heterogeneous populations are more robust than isolated compartments (functional redundancy via cross-feeding + horizontal transfer), with the anaerobic LUCA reconstruction as a far-end boundary rather than an assumption.

explanatory_gain.basis: Identifies robustness as an EMERGENT property bounded in (diversity x exchange) space — a phase boundary, not a monotone response — and frames the LUCA overlap as a reported constraint, separating "capabilities eventually acquired" from "the first compartments were LUCA-like".

limitations: The capability vector and its cross-feeding / horizontal-transfer / parasite dynamics are reduced couplings; the metacommunity is a deterministic coarse-grained reproduction, not a wrapped ALife engine and not N instantiated metabolic networks.

Each compartment reuses the og-02 protometabolic FUNCTION SET as a capability vector rather than running the libRoadRunner network per compartment; a genome-scale (COBRApy) benchmark of the emergent repertoire is deferred.

resolved_uncertainties: Connected, heterogeneous populations develop functional redundancy (robustness) that isolated compartments do not — robustly across seeds.
That robustness is an emergent property of a bounded (diversity x exchange) region, not a monotone response to either knob alone.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the emergent cross-feeding chains map onto specific reductive-TCA / Wood-Ljungdahl byproduct exchanges when the compartments run the real og-02 network.
How parasite load and network topology (beyond a ring) shift the emergence boundary.

followup_study_proposals.rationale: Instantiate the real og-02 libRoadRunner network per compartment for a small N and check the coarse-grained cross-feeding chains against metabolite exchange.
Carry the robust metacommunity into the escape-from-the-vent transition (dispersal to a fluctuating environment).
